He played [[college basketball]] for [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]] and [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]]. He is the son of [[Major League Baseball]] executive [[Omar Minaya]]. ==College career== Coming out of high school, Minaya was an unranked recruit but received several offers to play [[college basketball]]. He received official offers from [[South Carolina Gamecocks men's basketball|South Carolina]], [[UNC Wilmington Seahawks men's basketball|UNC Wilmington]], [[Boston University Terriers men's basketball|Boston University]], [[Illinois Fighting Illini men's basketball|Illinois]], [[Iona Gaels men's basketball|Iona]] and [[UMass Minutemen basketball|UMass]]. Minaya officially visited with South Carolina and UNC Wilmington before committing to South Carolina, signing his letter of intent on May 15, 2017. Minaya played four seasons with the Gamecocks from 2017 to 2021, only playing 5 games in 2018–19 due to a severe knee injury. In 2020, Minaya also underwent surgery on his thumb. He played all four years at South Carolina under head coach [[Frank Martin (basketball)|Frank Martin]]. After four years at South Carolina, Minaya transferred to [[Providence Friars men's basketball|Providence]] for his graduate season.{{cite web | title=Justin Minaya To Transfer To Providence From South Carolina | website=Providence College Athletics | date=2023-10-16 | url=https://friars.com/news/2021/5/3/mens-basketball-justin-minaya-to-transfer-to-providence-from-south-carolina | access-date=2025-12-05}} At Providence, Minaya averaged 6.5 points per game and started in 25 out of the 32 games he played in the 2021–22 season. The Friars won the Big East regular season championship in 2022 and advanced to Sweet 16 in the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], defeating [[South Dakota State Jackrabbits men's basketball|South Dakota State]] and [[Richmond Spiders men's basketball|Richmond]] before losing to [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]]. ==Professional career== ===Mexico City Capitanes (2022–2023)=== After going undrafted in the [[2022 NBA draft]], Minaya joined the [[Charlotte Hornets]] for the [[2022 NBA Summer League]].{{cite to the [[Mexico City Capitanes]]' roster to start the [[2022–23 NBA G League season]].{{cite web|title=2022-2023 Mexico City Capitanes Regular Season Minaya signed a 10-day contract with the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]{{cite web|first=Luke|last=Adams|title=Blazers Sign Justin Minaya For Rest Of Season|url=https://www.hoopsrumors.com/2023/04/blazers-sign-justin-minaya-for-rest-of-season.html|website=HoopsRumors.com|date=April 4, 2023|access-date=April 6, 2023}} and made his NBA debut that night, scoring 8 points in a 119–109 loss to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]].{{cite web|title=Justin Minaya|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/4278111/justin-minaya|website=ESPN.com|access-date=April re-signed with the Trail Blazers.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Sign Five Players|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-sign-five-players|website=NBA.com|date=October 2, 2023|access-date=October 4, 2023}} On October 21, 2023, his deal was converted to a [[two-way contract]] with the [[Rip City Remix]] of the [[NBA G League]].{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Convert Justin Minaya To Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-convert-justin-minaya-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=October 21, 2023|access-date=October 22, 2023}} On July 1, 2024, Minaya signed a second two-way contract with Portland.{{cite web|title=Trail Blazers Re-Sign Justin Minaya to Two-Way Contract|url=https://www.nba.com/blazers/news/trail-blazers-re-sign-justin-minaya-to-two-way-contract|website=NBA.com|date=July 1, 2024|access-date=July 2, 2024}} ===FC Barcelona (2026–present)=== After a season with the [[Osceola Magic]], Minaya signed with [[FC Barcelona Bàsquet|FC Barcelona]] of the [[Liga ACB]] and the [[EuroLeague]] on September 1, 2026.{{cite web|title=Justin Minaya strengthens blaugrana defense|url=https://www.fcbarcelona.com/en/basketball/first-team/news/4570030/justin-minaya-strengthens-blaugrana-defense|website=fcbarcelona.com|date=September 1,
